extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, third-party requesters, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners dealing with inter partes reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing oral hearings, Board decisions (including new grounds of rejection and remands), rehearing, post-decision processing, reopening prosecution, and appeals to the Federal Circuit in inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for oral hearing — filing, timing, and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant or a respondent desires an oral hearing, he or she must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must include a certification that a copy has been served in its entirety on all other parties and must indicate names and addresses of parties served. If no timely request and fee are filed, the appeal will be assigned and decided on the briefs without an oral hearing. No appellant or respondent will be permitted to participate in an oral hearing unless he or she has requested it and submitted the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing participation and argument time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, oral argument may be presented by or on behalf of the primary examiner if considered desirable. Oral argument will be limited to thirty minutes for each appellant or respondent who has requested an oral hearing, and twenty minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will set a non-extendable period within which other parties desiring to participate must submit requests. Only parties who have timely requested and paid may participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearings open to public observers and closure petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal involves reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers (subject to admittance procedures) unless an appellant and/or respondent petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open, presents sufficient reasons, pays the petition fee (37 CFR 41.20(a)), and the petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public observation is the default for reexamination appeals unless the formal petition and fee requirements are satisfied and granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on evidence and argument at oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, each appellant and respondent may only rely on evidence previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the briefs, except as permitted by paragraph (e)(2). The primary examiner may only rely on argument and evidence relied upon in an answer except as permitted by paragraph (e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New arguments or evidence are generally not permitted at oral hearing unless, upon a showing of good cause, a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court is presented. The Board will determine the order of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may decline to hold oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding a complying request for oral hearing, if the Board decides that a hearing is not necessary, the Board will so notify the owner and all requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a timely request and fee do not guarantee a hearing; the Board has discretion to decide that no hearing is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision scope — affirm, reverse, remand
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, in its decision, may affirm or reverse each decision of the examiner on all issues raised on each appealed claim, or remand the reexamination proceeding to the examiner for further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmance of a rejection constitutes general affirmance of the examiner's decision on that claim except as to any ground specifically reversed. Remand may be used where further consideration or procedure is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of examiner’s refusal to adopt third-party proposed rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The reversal of the examiner’s determination not to make a rejection proposed by the third party requester constitutes a decision adverse to the patentability of the claims which are subject to that proposed rejection and will be set forth in the Board’s decision as a new ground of rejection under paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reversal is treated as a new ground of rejection and triggers the special post-decision options for the patent owner; it also means the decision is not final for judicial review (when a new ground is included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may include new grounds of rejection (37 CFR 41.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board reverses the examiner’s determination or has knowledge of any grounds not raised in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include in its opinion a statement to that effect with its reasons, which statement shall constitute a new ground of rejection of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any decision including a new ground of rejection is not final for judicial review. When the Board makes a new ground, the owner, within one month from the date of the decision, must exercise one of two options to avoid termination: (1) reopen prosecution by filing an amendment/new evidence, or (2) request rehearing under § 41.79 addressing the new ground and stating with particularity the points misapprehended or overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner option — reopen prosecution after new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may file a response requesting reopening of prosecution before the examiner. Such a response must be either an amendment of the claims so rejected or new evidence relating to the claims so rejected, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening (37 CFR 41.77(b)(1)) allows the owner to amend claims or submit evidence under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132. Amendments/new claims must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims. Argument alone without amendment or new evidence can only result in the examiner maintaining the Board’s rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner option — request rehearing after new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may request that the proceeding be reheard under § 41.79 by the Board upon the same record. The request for rehearing must address any new ground of rejection and state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked and also state all other grounds upon which rehearing is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a rehearing request waives the owner's right to further prosecution before the examiner. The rehearing request must comply with § 41.79(b) and be filed within the one-month non-extendable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester comments after owner response (limited scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the owner has filed a response requesting reopening of prosecution, any requester, within one month of the date of service of the owner’s response, may once file comments on the response. Such comments must be limited to the issues raised by the Board’s opinion reflecting its decision and the owner’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester that had not previously filed an appeal or cross appeal and seeks to file comments/reply is subject to appeal and brief fees under § 41.20(b)(1) and (2), which must accompany the comments or reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to examiner and examiner’s obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Following any owner response and any requester comments, the proceeding will be remanded to the examiner. The statement of the Board shall be binding upon the examiner unless an amendment or new evidence not previously of record is made which, in the opinion of the examiner, overcomes the new ground of rejection stated in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will consider owner response and requester comments and issue a determination that the rejection is maintained or has been overcome. The proceeding then continues under normal examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extensions for owner response and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The time period set forth for the owner to respond to a new ground (paragraph (b)) is subject to the extension provisions of § 1.956 when the owner is responding under paragraph (b)(1). The time period may not be extended when the owner is responding under paragraph (b)(2). The time periods for filing requester comments and replies (paragraphs (c) and (e)) may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under § 1.956 are available for reopening prosecution responses but are limited in total (see MPEP guidance). The one-month periods for rehearing and many comment windows are non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing request content and restrictions (37 CFR 41.79(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked in rendering the Board’s opinion. Arguments not raised in the briefs before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon in the briefs are not permitted in the request for rehearing except as permitted by paragraphs (b)(2) and (b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon a showing of good cause, parties may present a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of the Board or a Federal Court. New arguments responding to a new ground of rejection are permitted. The one-month filing period is non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposing comments to rehearing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of the date of service of any request for rehearing, the owner and all requesters may once file comments in opposition to the request for rehearing. The comments in opposition must be limited to the issues raised in the request for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comment window is once-only and non-extendable; comments must be confined to rehearing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision on rehearing — incorporation and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party files a request for rehearing, the Board shall render a decision on the request. The decision on the request for rehearing is deemed to incorporate the earlier opinion reflecting its decision for appeal, except for those portions specifically withdrawn on rehearing, and is final for the purpose of judicial review, except when noted otherwise in the decision on rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board’s rehearing opinion becomes a new decision, parties may file a further request for rehearing within one month of that new decision, subject to the same particularity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rehearing rights before appeal to Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties to an appeal may not appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit under § 1.983 until all parties’ rights to request rehearing have been exhausted, at which time the decision of the Board is final and appealable by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing rights must be exhausted (or deadlines lapsed) before initiating an appeal to the Federal Circuit; timing rules and non-extendable periods apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening after final Board decision (Director consent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision by the Board has become final for judicial review, prosecution of the inter partes reexamination proceeding will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under the provisions of § 41.77 without the written authority of the Director, and then only for the consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening after finality is rare and requires Director written authority; reopening is limited to matters not already adjudicated and where sufficient cause is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU processing and timing after Board decision; NIRC issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: After an appeal has been decided, a copy of the decision is mailed to all parties, the original is placed in the file, and the clerk forwards the file to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) immediately if the examiner is reversed, and after about six weeks if the examiner is affirmed or after a rehearing decision is rendered. The CRU processes the decision and forwards the file to the examiner via the CRU Director so that a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) can be issued to terminate the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.67.01 is used when NIRC is issued. The CRU staff uses the Board decision to prepare appropriate amendments and cancellations in the NIRC and to instruct the examiner on claim status.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC handling of claims and examples (dependent/ amended claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIRC will indicate the status of all claims as a result of the Board decision. Claims refused are red-lined and noted 'Board Decision.' Claims indicated as patentable prior to appeal except for their dependency from rejected claims not in the original patent will be treated as if they were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) If claim 10 was amended/added and claim 11 depends on 10, and the Board affirms rejection of 10 and 11 was patentable only due to dependency, cancel both claims by formal examiner's amendment attached to NIRC. (2) If both 10 and 11 were rejected prior to appeal and the Board affirms 10 but reverses 11, the examiner should convert dependent claim 11 into independent form by formal amendment and cancel claim 10; examiner may set a one-month/30-day time to rewrite dependent claim 11 in independent form with extensions under 37 CFR 1.956 allowed; if no timely response, cancel both claims in the NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board cannot recommend explicit amendment to make claim allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike ex parte practice, the Board's decision in inter partes reexamination cannot include an explicit statement that a claim may be allowed in amended form such that the patent owner would have the right to amend in conformity and it would be binding on the examiner in the absence of new references or grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remark that a certain feature does not appear in a claim is not to be taken as a recommendation that the claim be allowed if the feature is supplied by amendment. Permitting such a recommendation would complicate patent owner and third-party response rights late in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may suspend consideration pending court action
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the Board has refused to consider an appeal until after the conclusion of a pending civil action or appeal to the Federal Circuit involving issues identical with, or similar to, those presented in the later appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is recognized as sound practice where a court decision may be determinative of issues involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection — scope of 'reopening prosecution'
rubrics_metrics.description: The new ground of rejection raised by the Board does not 'reopen the prosecution' except as to that subject matter to which the new rejection was applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment or showing of facts not directed to the subject matter to which the new rejection was applied will be refused entry and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) on ACP/RAN and reopening without CRU Director consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1) in effect nullifies the ACP and RAN and automatically reopens the prosecution of the subject matter of the claims so rejected by the Board. Accordingly, the written consent of the CRU Director is not required on the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, written consent of the CRU Director is required for reopening prosecution where the reexamination proceeding was remanded for failure to follow procedure, to provide more information, or to consider something not yet considered, and the examiner then concludes a change in position is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU Director and Director of the USPTO discretion on petitions to reopen
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU Director will decide petitions to reopen prosecution of an inter partes reexamination proceeding after Board decision where no court action has been filed. The Director of the USPTO entertains petitions to reopen certain cases in which an appellant has sought court review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure is restricted to cases amenable to settlement without going forward with the court proceeding; reopening in these circumstances is exceptional and discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Federal Circuit — who may appeal and procedural steps (37 CFR 1.983)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner, or a third-party requester in an inter partes reexamination proceeding who is a party to an appeal to the Board and who is dissatisfied with the Board decision, may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps the appellant must take: (1) timely file a written notice of appeal in the USPTO directed to the Director in accordance with §§ 1.302 and 1.304; (2) in the Federal Circuit, file a copy of the notice of appeal and pay the fee as provided by the court; and (3) serve a copy of the notice of appeal on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in § 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-appeals and participation in appeals to the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner files a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit, the third party requester may cross appeal if dissatisfied, and vice versa. A party electing to participate in an appellant’s appeal must, within fourteen days of service of the appellant’s notice of appeal or notice of cross appeal, take specified steps to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation steps: (1) in the USPTO, timely file a written notice directed to the Director electing to participate (by mail or hand to the General Counsel per § 104.2); (2) in the Federal Circuit, file a copy of the notice electing to participate per court rules; and (3) serve a copy of the notice on every other party per § 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions for reexaminations commenced before November 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any provision of the rules, in any reexamination proceeding commenced prior to November 2, 2002, the third party requester is precluded from appealing and cross appealing any decision of the Board to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, and is precluded from participating in any appeal taken by the patent owner to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a jurisdictional/temporal restriction that limits third-party requester appellate rights in older proceedings.
